entities.text: COMMON JUDGMENT K.G.Sunil vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
These appeals and Cross objections arise out of a joint trial by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Ernakulam in OP (MV) Nos.1931 of 2016, 1028 of 2016 & 1027 of 2016.

2. The brief facts necessary for the disposal of the appeals are as follows:-
On 23.11.2015 at 11.20 pm, while the deceased, Sudheesh S., Athul Raj and Mohammed Sameer, were travelling as passengers in a Tavera bearing Registration No.KL- 41-4292 through Ponnani - Edappal SH road from west to east, when the vehicle reached at Biyyam bridge, Ponnani, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle, the vehicle hit against an electric post and a MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 tree and the vehicle capsized which resulted in the death of the three passengers, who were minors.
The deceased victims were bright young students with the blossoming career prospects and were on the verge of completing their 10th class.

O.P.(M.V.) No.1027 of 2016 is preferred by the legal heirs of deceased Sudheesh S, OP (M.V.) No.1028 of 2016 by the legal heirs of the Athul Raj and finally O.P. (M.V.) No.1931 of 2016 is preferred by Muhammed Sameer, who later succumbed to the injuries during the pendency of the trial and later the legal heirs were impleaded and claimed compensation on account of death.
3. The basic issue that arises in these appeals and Cross objections is with regard to the notional income liable to be fixed in respect of the minor students.

The tribunal on appreciation of the rival contentions fixed the notional income at Rs.10,000/- which according to the appellants are insufficient, whereas the insurance company has preferred Cross objections contending that the fixation of the notional income at Rs.10,000/- is on a MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022,
MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 higher side.

entities.text: MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Incidentally in O.P.(M.V.) No.1931 of 2016 from which MACA No.1558 of 2021 arises there is a claim for enhancement of compensation under the head pain and sufferings since it is stated that the deceased Mohammed Sameer had been hospitalized for nearly one year and thereafter succumbed to the injuries.
4. Heard Sri. V.A. Omanakuttan, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants/appellants and Sri. P. Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing counsel appearing for the insurance company/Cross objectors.

5. On consideration of the rival submissions raised across the bar, this Court finds that the appeals preferred by the claimants have to be allowed and the cross objections preferred by the insurance company are liable to be dismissed on the following reasons:-
6. The Cross objection is preferred primarily contending that the notional income of the minor cannot be fixed and loss of dependency cannot be calculated by applying a multiplier system, even if the income of a MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of K.G.Sunil vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133422555/
9 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 deceased minor has to be fixed.

entities.text: K.G.Sunil vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the insurance company, the same ought to be fixed annually and not as a monthly income.

It is further contended that the parents alone are entitled to the consortium and on that ground also, the award of the tribunal is liable to be modified.
7.

Coming to the appeals preferred by the claimants, this Court must notice that all the three minor children who died in the road traffic accident were outstanding in the field of Sports and also were bright in their studies.
8. The evidence in these case consists of Exts.A1 to A11 in O.P.(M.V.) No.1027 of 2016, Exts.A12 to A39, A62 & A63 in O.P.(M.V.) No.1028 of 2016, Exts.A40 to A56 in O.P.(M.V.) No.1931 of 2016.
These records equally evidences the outstanding ability of the students and also their bright future.
The claimants were further successful in establishing these prospects by examining PW1 to PW4.

Therefore, the only question that remains before this Court is whether the notional income fixed by the tribunal in so MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 far as the three minor students were concerned is proper or not.

9. On a reading of the award impugned in the appeal shows that the tribunal has followed the principles laid down in M. Ramachandrappa Vs. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance insurance company [AIR 2011 SC 2951].

entities.text: M. Ramachandrappa Vs. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance insurance company [AIR 2011 SC 2951]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, while doing so, the tribunal seems to have failed to recognize the well settled principle that while fixing the notional income of a student they cannot be equated with that of a coolie worker.
The student has to be recognized under the category of skilled worker.

10. In Angad Tiwari Vs. National insurance company [2024 KHC 8590] the Hon'ble Supreme Court categorically held that while fixing income of a claim under Section 166, the tribunal and the Courts shall not fix the same below the minimum wage.

entities.text: Angad Tiwari Vs. National insurance company [2024 KHC 8590]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In the facts of the present case this Court is however faced with a predicament since there is no guiding factor in the form of the notification issued by the MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 State of Kerala under the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act.
Although, the State had issued G.O.(P) No. 28/2016/Fin dated 26.02.2016 the same effected from 01.04.2016.
The learned counsel for the appellant would however point out that nothing prevents this Court from adopting the criteria fixed by the State Government in the aforesaid notification.

However it is to be noted that the date of accident in the present case is 23.11.2015 whereas the notification takes effect only from 01.04.2016 and therefore the notification as such cannot be applied and the notional income cannot be fixed in terms of the minimum wage contained therein.

12. However, this Court is of the considered view that by itself, need not deter this Court from proceeding to fix the notional income on suitable terms by applying suitable deductions from the minimum wage that is fixed under G.O.(P) No.28/16/Fin. dated 26.02.2016.

This is, primarily for the reason that the tribunal also fixed the notional income based on the principles laid down in K.G.Sunil vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133422555/
10 MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:

entities.text: K.G.Sunil vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: M. Ramachandrappa (supra).
However, while doing so, the tribunal failed to notice the fact that the income of the student cannot be equated with that of a coolie worker.
Turning to G.O.(P) No.28/2016/Fin., this Court finds that the minimum wage liable to be paid to a skilled workman is Rs.17,550/-.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that a suitable income could be determined by applying a suitable deduction of 15% from Rs.17,550/-.

By adopting the aforesaid formula, this Court finds that by applying 15% deduction, the amount will come to Rs.14,917/- and it is rounded off to Rs.15,000/- and accordingly notional income of the minor students are fixed at Rs.15,000/-, the claimants should also be entitled to 15%
future prospects on the aforesaid amount.

13. In so far as MACA No.1558 of 2021 is concerned, this Court needs to address the contention of the learned counsel for the appellants that the deceased Mohammed Sameer was treated as an inpatient in Amala Institute of Medical Science from 24.11.15 to 16.12.2015 MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744
thereafter he was admitted in City Hospital, Ernakulam from 16.12.2015 to 02.01.2016.
Again the deceased Muhammed Sameer was admitted to Indo American Hospital from 03.1.2016 to 18.06.16.
Thus, it is seen that for more than 8 months, the deceased Mohammed Sameer was undergoing treatments in various hospitals.
It is raised across the bar that altogether 208 days the deceased as Muhammed Sameer was hospitalized.

However, on perusal of the structure of compensation granted by the tribunal, it is revealed that the appellants have been granted only an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for pain and suffering which requires to be enhanced reasonably.
Accordingly, the appellants are granted an additional sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering.
14. Before parting this appeal, it seems, this Court needs to address one more issue raised by the learned counsel for the insurance company.
According to the insurance company, the tribunal had granted compensation to all the claimants other than parents.

Thus, MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 according to the insurance company the parental consortium alone is liable to be granted.
However, this Court does not find any merit in the aforesaid contention especially since the claimants other than parents are the siblings of the deceased minor students.

It is settled law that the siblings are entitled for compensation under the head love and affection if not, under the head loss of consortium and therefore to that extent, this Court does not find it appropriate to reduce the amount granted under the head love and affection.

15. As an upshot of the above discussions, this Court finds that all the appeals preferred by the claimants are liable to be allowed and the Cross objections preferred by the insurance company are liable to be dismissed.
16. Thus, the appeals are allowed and the income of the deceased minor students are re-fixed at Rs.15,000/- with 40% future prospects as sought by them, thus a total amount of Rs.21,000/- is fixed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The deceased victims were bright young students with the blossoming career prospects and were on the verge of completing their 10th class.
O.P.(M.V.) No.1027 of 2016 is preferred by the legal heirs of deceased Sudheesh S, OP (M.V.) No.1028 of 2016 by the legal heirs of the Athul Raj and finally O.P. (M.V.) No.1931 of 2016 is preferred by Muhammed Sameer, who later succumbed to the injuries during the pendency of the trial and later the legal heirs were impleaded and claimed compensation on account of death.
9. On a reading of the award impugned in the appeal shows that the tribunal has followed the principles laid down in M. Ramachandrappa Vs. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance insurance company [AIR 2011 SC 2951].
However, while doing so, the tribunal seems to have failed to recognize the well settled principle that while fixing the notional income of a student they cannot be equated with that of a coolie worker.
opennyai_summary.issue:
3. The basic issue that arises in these appeals and Cross objections is with regard to the notional income liable to be fixed in respect of the minor students.
Therefore, the only question that remains before this Court is whether the notional income fixed by the tribunal in so MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 far as the three minor students were concerned is proper or not.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
5. On consideration of the rival submissions raised across the bar, this Court finds that the appeals preferred by the claimants have to be allowed and the cross objections preferred by the insurance company are liable to be dismissed on the following reasons:-
6. The Cross objection is preferred primarily contending that the notional income of the minor cannot be fixed and loss of dependency cannot be calculated by applying a multiplier system, even if the income of a MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of K.G.Sunil vs The New India Assurance Co Ltd on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133422555/
9 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 deceased minor has to be fixed.
The student has to be recognized under the category of skilled worker.
However it is to be noted that the date of accident in the present case is 23.11.2015 whereas the notification takes effect only from 01.04.2016 and therefore the notification as such cannot be applied and the notional income cannot be fixed in terms of the minimum wage contained therein.
12. However, this Court is of the considered view that by itself, need not deter this Court from proceeding to fix the notional income on suitable terms by applying suitable deductions from the minimum wage that is fixed under G.O.(P) No.28/16/Fin. dated 26.02.2016.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. In Angad Tiwari Vs. National insurance company [2024 KHC 8590] the Hon'ble Supreme Court categorically held that while fixing income of a claim under Section 166, the tribunal and the Courts shall not fix the same below the minimum wage.
11. In the facts of the present case this Court is however faced with a predicament since there is no guiding factor in the form of the notification issued by the MACA No.1558 of 2021 & CO No.194 of 2022, MACA No.892 of 2021 & CO No.70 of 2021, & MACA No.1038 of 2021 & CO No.1 of 2023 2025:KER:32744 State of Kerala under the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act.
Although, the State had issued G.O.(P) No. 28/2016/Fin dated 26.02.2016 the same effected from 01.04.2016.
It is settled law that the siblings are entitled for compensation under the head love and affection if not, under the head loss of consortium and therefore to that extent, this Court does not find it appropriate to reduce the amount granted under the head love and affection.

16. Thus, the appeals are allowed and the income of the deceased minor students are re-fixed at Rs.15,000/- with 40% future prospects as sought by them, thus a total amount of Rs.21,000/- is fixed.
The Loss of dependency in all theses cases will stand modified as follows:
Loss of dependency 21000 x 12 x 15 x 1/2= 18,90,000 - 12,60,000= 6,30,000/-
17.
In addition to the above, the claimants in OP(MV) No.1931 of 2016 are awarded a further sum of Rs.100,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
